Net map: n1 = top of I-AC 2 (arrow up) -> up to the corner at (120,150) -> right into the left end of Resistor 0 (2k); n2 = right end of Resistor 0 -> left end of Inductor 1 (2mH); n3 = the upper right node: right end of Inductor 1 -> T at (282,177) (verified at 8x: the capacitor column starts there and only goes down, the rail passes on) -> the rail continues right and down-slanting to the corner at (355,192) -> down into the top of Resistor 6 (5k); the same T also feeds down into the top plate of Capacitor 3; n4 = bottom plate of Capacitor 3 -> down into the top of Resistor 4 (2k) (the two are in series in the centre column, confirmed at 7x); n5 = bottom of Resistor 6 -> top of Inductor 7 (10mH), also a plain series link in the right column; 0 = bottom rail, running from the bottom-left corner at (93,278) down-right to (329,327): it carries the bottom of I-AC 2, the bottom of Resistor 4, GND 5 and the bottom of Inductor 7. Judgment calls: (a) at (256,312) the centre column crosses the bottom rail and continues a few pixels further down into the GND 5 bar stack at y=321..328 - that is a 4-way junction, not a crossover (there is no hop and the GND has to attach to something), so the whole bottom rail plus the GND is one net '0'; (b) every other meeting in this circuit is a plain T or corner; there are no dots, hops or crossovers anywhere; (c) the dashes in the rails are binarisation dropout of one continuous faint line - the same dash pattern runs through stretches where nothing else is drawn; (d) I-AC 2's arrow points up so index 0 is its top terminal; Capacitor 3 is indexed top-then-bottom, Resistors 4 and 6 and Inductor 7 top-then-bottom, Resistor 0 and Inductor 1 left-then-right, all as drawn - 2-terminal order affects no metric; (e) the bootstrap left I-AC 2, Capacitor 3 and half of Resistor 6 / Inductor 7 null and invented n5/n6/n7 for the centre and right columns; R0 and L1's bootstrap nets were the only correct ones.
